also_changed.change: tools/validate_skills.py now warns when a row cites a kb id under the same verbatim quote as the root contract or one of the skill's own builds_on skills, without naming that skill anywhere in the row. Keying on the pair (id, quote) is what distinguishes a restated fact from a sibling citing the same record for its own point: the first cut, keyed on the id alone, produced 140 warnings and was retuned to 40 before being kept. One line per skill and id however many rows repeat it. It is a warning, not an error, because a genuine independent citation can trip it; the brief tells authors to read each one.

decisions.problem: The first cut of the compose-by-name check keyed on the kb id alone and produced 140 warnings on a 15-skill tree, most of them a use/implement sibling legitimately citing the same primary record for its own point. A check that noisy is a check nobody reads, and it would have buried the 112 'not written yet' warnings that authors do act on.
options: Drop the check and leave compose-by-name to the brief - rejected: the rule has been in the brief through three ceremonies and was still missed twice in wave 2.

Keep the check but key it on the pair (kb id, verbatim quote), since copying a fact reproduces the owner's quote while an independent citation of the same record usually quotes a different sentence for a different point - taken: it cut the output from 140 to 40 rows, each a genuine same-id-same-quote overlap, and it is the pattern all three ceremony findings had (F-a7-03, F-a7-04, F-b1-08/F-b4-01 each restated under the root contract's own quote).

Make it an error rather than a warning - rejected: a sibling can legitimately quote the same sentence, so an error would block correct work; the brief instead requires the author to read each warning and either name the owner or justify the row.
decisions.chosen: Keyed on (id, quote), deduplicated to one line per skill and id, kept as a warning, and documented in the brief's budget paragraph and defect item 2.
decisions.quote: define the problem, identify the three best possible solutions that align to the goal, and follow the recommendation

decisions.problem: The new budget warning reports two wave-1 skills at 13 instructions (build-adapter-pair, build-skill-authoring) that ceremony 1 reviewed and closed without counting. They are outside this ceremony's section.
options: Merge their tables now - rejected: it rewrites skills a closed ceremony accepted, in a section this ceremony did not review, and the churn would land in the same commit as the wave-2 fixes with no reviewer having read it.
Silence the warning for skills written before the check existed - rejected: it hides the only evidence that the check earns its place.

Leave the warning standing, record the two skills here, and let the next ceremony that reviews them apply the merge - taken: the warning now makes them impossible to miss, and the fix lands with a review behind it.
decisions.chosen: Recorded here and left visible in the validator output; build-adapter-pair and build-skill-authoring carry 13 instructions each and are the next section's merge candidates. This is not a known-issues entry: they are warnings, not errors, and nothing builds on a broken skill.
decisions.quote: define the problem, identify the three best possible solutions that align to the goal, and follow the recommendation

lessons_for_next_section: A defect that recurs in three consecutive ceremonies is a missing check, not an author's mistake: write it into the validator, not into the brief a third time.
Tune a new check against the tree you have before keeping it; keying compose-by-name on (kb id, verbatim quote) instead of the id alone took it from 140 unreadable warnings to 40 real overlaps.
Compose by name is checked per citation, not per skill: both wave-2 offenders stated the same finding correctly elsewhere in the same file.
State an enumeration once per skill and point every other row at that list; and name which enumeration you cite, since TARGET.md T1 lists three ways in and T6.2 lists four entries.
A budget nothing checks is not a budget: the new warning found two wave-1 skills at 13 instructions that two ceremonies had read past.
An instruction-table overrun is two steps that are one act; both wave-2 overruns merged with no claim and no citation dropped.
Ceremony numbers stayed repo-global under a second collision: the harness handed number 2 again, the review and this record took 3, and nothing closed was overwritten.
